bounds.domain: One exact native SMS or MMS bridge call and its pending owner, one worker journal lookup, one main-queue native dialog, one owner Send tap, one queued dispatch, and one cancellation or foreground retirement. At most one platform invocation and one result; fixed operation and binding identity.
bounds.projection: The call owner exists before the journal work is queued and remains until the original call resolves or rejects. Cancellation marks matching outstanding owners before its own acknowledgement. A retired owner cannot open a later dialog or dispatch after a Send tap waits on the worker. A recorded or admitted result is retained through cancellation. An unrelated operation cannot retire this owner.
bounds.conformance: The mandatory Android Gradle check compiles the real TelephonyPlugin and SmsTelephony and executes actual bridge methods under Robolectric29 with controlled worker/Main queues, a granted test foreground/SIM and an in-memory native journal. Six new cases exercise initial SMS/MMS cancellation, lifecycle retirement, cancellation after Send, unrelated cancellation, and already recorded submission readback. The existing SMS/MMS journal suites also execute; exact testcase names and zero skips are required.
bounds.limits: The state model is a finite native queue boundary projection, not a refinement proof. The single abstract invocation does not enumerate multipart or multi-recipient partial sends. Native journal suites supplement those cases. Simultaneous independent hosts, arbitrary Android lifecycle delivery, storage write failures, callback batching/listener fanout, carrier/provider acceptance, real SIM roles/permissions and physical Android foreground-service behavior are outside this projection. Robolectric ports prove no radio or carrier delivery.

assumptions: No fairness. Cancellation is processed on Main after the pending owner is registered and before its own bridge acknowledgement.
No fairness. A known result already admitted by the exact journal is not rolled back by retirement.
Weak fairness of journal lookup return and cancelled-call journal settlement. A previously dispatched call remains owned by its native completion; no provider completion is assumed.
No fairness or owner response. A journal lookup, owner dialog or native callback may remain pending forever.
